reviews.text: My quest to quit. This will be my third attempt to quit smoking I have quit before with this app for about 3 yrs... I fell off the again this year for about 2-3 months and had to quit again and knew I could only do it with this app showing me my progress and why I'm doing it!! Thank you QuitNow for helping me again on my journey to quit smoking. I'm currently on day 22 and not looking back.

GAME CHANGER!. I tried quitting many, many times as have many people. I am a competitive person when it comes to activities but also competitive with myself to thrive and rise above plateaus for myself. Nothing I tried worked. I tried the vaping and that was just almost more addictive and just as bad for you even though people think it’s safe. I didn’t want to put any more of the toxins into my body so I really wanted to quit cold turkey and I was not successful and I heard about this app and it changed my life. Being able to check in every day or every hour or every minute if I had to to look at my progress helped keep me motivated to keep moving forward. I still have moments where I just want to go to the store and get cigarettes but it passes pretty fast and I’m almost at two years and I definitely know I will never smoke again even. I also know that being a lifelong smoker I will probably crave it throughout my whole life but all I need to do is look at this app to see my progress.

The paid app does more, but I haven’t seemed to need it. I think the Chantix is key to successfully quitting. I’ve made it 7.5 days with no cigarettes! 

My wife is thrilled!

Don’t buy PRO. It’s just not worth it. Thankfully, it’s cheap, so I’m not to worried about it, but wanted to warn others. My biggest complaint is that people are depending on accurate health information, yet it’s highly inaccurate. After paying for the app you get provided with misinformation, such as, in about 5 years your risk of getting lung cancer will decrease to that of a non-smoker. Right under that lie, is a statement declaring they receive their information from W.H.O. Well, realizing it’s going to take much longer than 5 years to decrease my risk of lung cancer to such an extent, if at all, I went to the W.H.O. website to verify this information. There you learn, it takes 10 years to decrease your risk of lung cancer just by HALF. Also, it takes between 2-12 weeks to increase lung function and circulation, NOT 2 days as the app claims. There are others, but I’m over texting this review now.
